clue.text: Repeat performance from soldier in English army section

indicators.note: in tells us the soldier is placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
an NCO, a non-commissioned officer, is a soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier performs again for part of the British army.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NCO inside E and RE. RE is the Royal Engineers, a branch of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra piece played when the audience calls for more is literally a repeat performance.

clue.text: Continental regret over article brought into public domain?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word for regret is turned upward, read backwards

parts.note: to rue is to regret

indicators.note: brought into means the article goes inside the word for public

parts.note: open means public, available to all
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone regrets an article that has entered the public domain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns RUE into EUR; 'brought into' puts A inside OPEN to give OPEAN. 'domain' is padding for the surface and does no job in the wordplay beyond the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Continental, in British usage, means belonging to mainland Europe, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Spell attractiveness

definitions.meaning: the quality of being pleasing or alluring

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a magic spell and personal appeal, two separate senses of one noun.

clue.text: Small state with old port

parts.note: RI is Rhode Island, the smallest US state

explanation.surface: A small state has an ancient harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian seaport, so it is an example of a port.

clue.text: A thick-coated dog or two

parts.note: the breed name is a dog's short name doubled, so one such dog looks like two of them written side by side

explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese breed has a dense, thick coat and a blue-black tongue.

clue.text: Food bound for Tamworth? Nonsense

definitions.meaning: Tamworth is a British pig breed, so its food is pigswill

explanation.walkthrough: Tamworth is a town in England but also a ginger breed of pig; the question mark marks that second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Swill fed to pigs gives its name to talk that is rubbish, a figurative sense.

clue.text: Equivocation leads to row, primarily with artist's supporter

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of the word with is used
leads to means the earlier pieces come before the next one

parts.note: an easel holds up an artist's canvas
a row, a quarrel, is having words

explanation.surface: Being evasive causes an argument, mostly involving the painter's backer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes W from 'with'; 'leads to' says W and EASEL come before WORDS. 'Words' means a quarrel, as in 'we had words'.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately ambiguous phrases used to avoid commitment are the stuff of equivocation.

clue.text: Switch tune in Haydn's first composition

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of Haydn is taken

parts.note: an air is a tune
a piece is a musical composition

explanation.surface: A melody appears in Haydn's first work.
explanation.walkthrough: A switch is a tress of false hair, a sense many solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a length of false hair worn to add bulk, so a kind of wig.

clue.text: Roam with 1 dn, falling into wide river

indicators.note: falling into means the middle pieces drop inside the outer ones

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
and means with, in addition to
the answer to 1 down means European, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: Someone wanders off with a European and falls into a broad river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falling into' puts AND plus E inside W and R. '1 dn' points to the answer at 1 Down, European, whose abbreviation is E.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to travel about without a fixed route, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Settled on some form of prayer

parts.note: lit, as a bird lit on a branch, means settled
any means some, as in 'have you any?'

explanation.surface: Someone decides on a certain kind of prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of petitions with set responses, a form of prayer in church.

clue.text: Train of thought of each boy in band

indicators.note: in means the pieces before it go inside the band

parts.note: a ring is a band
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: Thinking about each lad in a musical group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts EA and SON inside RING; 'band' looks musical but means a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of logical argument from step to step is a train of thought.

clue.text: Stranger removing edges from part of defence work

indicators.note: removing edges from means the first and last letters of the fortification term are dropped

parts.note: a salient is a projecting part of a fortification

explanation.surface: An outsider trims the ends from a section of fortifications.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removing edges from' drops S and T from SALIENT, a jutting part of a defensive line.
explanation.definitionFit: An alien is a foreigner or outsider, so a stranger.

clue.text: Fruit nana consumed with maiden in 14

indicators.note: in means the maiden goes inside the answer to 14

parts.note: the answer to 14 Across, the thriller writer
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over
nana and gran are both names for a grandmother
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Grandma eats a piece of fruit with a young girl inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts M inside POE (14 Across) to give POME; M for maiden comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fruit with leathery skin full of juicy red seeds, so an example.

clue.text: Single gambler supports attempt to achieve superior performance

indicators.note: in a down clue, supports means the following pieces sit below the attempt

parts.note: a go is an attempt
one means single
a better is one who bets

explanation.surface: A lone punter backs a try to outdo someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' places ONE BETTER below GO, since a down entry reads from the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone by doing slightly more is to achieve a superior performance, an idiom.

clue.text: Bard has no time for thriller writer

indicators.note: has no means the time letter is taken away from the bard

parts.note: a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: A poet is impatient with a writer of thrillers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no' removes T from POET. Edgar Allan Poe wrote early mystery and horror tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe wrote tales of mystery and terror, so he fits as a writer of thrillers.

clue.text: Unknown bloke in a US city?

definitions.text: Unknown bloke in a US city?

parts.words: Unknown bloke in a US city?
parts.note: an unnamed person is any person

explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means any person at all, so an unidentified bloke.

clue.text: Description of Chichester hospital with many cats loose outside

indicators.note: outside means the anagram goes around the hospital letter
loose means the letters of many cats are set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital in Chichester, surrounded by many stray cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' rearranges MANY CATS and 'outside' puts that around H. Sir Francis Chichester sailed alone round the world in 1966-67; Chichester is also an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Chichester was a famous solo sailor, so the word describes him.

clue.text: Glaring mistake made by schoolboy identifying monkey

definitions.meaning: a blunder, the classic schoolboy gaffe
a South American monkey with a loud call

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a laughable blunder and a loud-calling American monkey.

clue.text: Awkward situation, meeting getting into paper!

indicators.note: getting into means the meeting goes inside the paper

parts.note: a quire is a measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
AGM is an annual general meeting

explanation.surface: A tricky moment as a meeting gets reported in the newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts AGM inside QUIRE; 'paper' suggests a newspaper but means sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog that traps you is used figuratively for a predicament, an awkward situation.

clue.text: Fit into approach to building

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a sudden outburst of feeling and a means of entry.

clue.text: Tricky cunning disheartened special crew

indicators.note: disheartened means the middle of the word special is removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: A crafty plan discourages an elite team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' keeps only the first and last letters of 'special', S and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity used to deceive, as in sleight of hand, so trickery.

clue.text: Social climber's standard meeting-place out East

parts.note: par is a standard level

indicators.note: out means the East letter is removed from the meeting-place

parts.note: a venue is a meeting-place

explanation.surface: An upstart's usual haunt lies in the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes E from VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is someone who has risen socially but lacks breeding, an upstart.

clue.text: Contemptible crony put to the test.

parts.note: a pal is a crony
to try is to put to the test

explanation.surface: Testing a friend is a mean thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trivial or worthless, deserving contempt, a close synonym.

clue.text: Language a priest used to enter bravery award

indicators.note: to enter means the pieces go inside the bravery award

parts.note: GC is the George Cross, a British award for gallantry
Eli is the priest in the Bible who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A clergyman uses words to receive a medal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to enter' puts A and ELI inside GC, the George Cross, a British gallantry award.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaelic is the Celtic language of Scotland and Ireland, so an example of a language.

clue.text: Having a tendency to be clever

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means inclined to something and also quick or able at learning.

clue.text: Eternal description of the rest Romeo set up here?

definitions.text: description of the rest Romeo set up here?
definitions.meaning: in Romeo and Juliet, Romeo in the tomb vows to set up his rest there for all time

explanation.walkthrough: The second half quotes Romeo and Juliet, Act 5 Scene 3, where Romeo, about to die in the tomb, describes the rest he will set up there.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means lasting forever, a direct synonym of the first sense.

clue.text: From domed hut, head off big game

indicators.note: head off means the first letter of the word big is removed

parts.note: loo is an old card game

explanation.surface: Big game hunting begins from a domed shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' drops B from 'big', leaving IG. LOO is a card game, not the British toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dwelling of snow blocks with a domed roof, so a domed hut.

clue.text: Bound to be inflamed about note

indicators.note: about means the inflamed word wraps around the note

parts.note: lit means set alight, inflamed
mi is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Sure to get angry over a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts MI inside LIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound is a boundary or furthest extent, so the noun sense is a synonym.

clue.text: Blouse made by hairless person in Indiana city, say?

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken and its sound gives the entry

parts.note: a baldy is a bald person, and Gary is a city in Indiana

explanation.surface: A shirt produced by a bald man from a Midwestern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' means 'Gary baldy', a bald man from Gary, sounds like the entry. A Garibaldi is a loose blouse styled on the red shirts of Garibaldi's soldiers; also a British currant biscuit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Garibaldi is a loose high-necked blouse modelled on the red shirts of Garibaldi's soldiers.

clue.text: In Mississippi, measure shoal at mouth of river

definitions.meaning: a unit of music between two vertical lines
a sandbank across a river mouth

explanation.walkthrough: 'In Mississippi' sets the river scene: sandbars form at the Mississippi's mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a musical measure and a sandbank across a river mouth.

clue.text: Worn-out old lag initially full of remorse

indicators.note: initially means the convict comes first, before the worn-out word

parts.note: a con, convict, is an old lag
trite means worn-out, hackneyed

explanation.surface: A tired former prisoner feels deeply sorry at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' puts CON in front of TRITE. Old lag is British slang for a habitual prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite means feeling sorrow for wrongdoing, so remorseful.

clue.text: Trendy to be in this settled routine?

explanation.definitionFit: The word gives the idiom for being fashionable and also means a fixed routine or rut.
